lines.text: Emails start with I am writing!
Many learners say: I write to you to ask about the job.
Better: I am writing to you to ask about the job.
Am writing! I am writing to ask about a job.

data.wrong: I write to you to ask about the job.
data.right: I am writing to you to ask about the job.

quiz.stem: Hello, I ___ to ask about a job.

native.tip: En español “le escribo para…” va en presente, pero en un correo en inglés se dice “I am writing to you.”
native.caption: Muchos dicen “I write to you to ask about the job.” 🙈 En español “le escribo para…” va en presente simple, pero en un correo en inglés se dice: “I am writing to you to ask about the job.” ¡Escucha a Carlos y repite! Practica más en la app Lexkite.
native.comment: Respuesta: “am writing”. En un correo, “I am writing to…” suena natural. Escribe una frase tuya con “am writing”. Practica más con un quiz gratis aquí: {link}

en.hook: “I write to you”? Say it better.
en.tip: In Spanish “le escribo para…” uses the simple present, but in an English email we say “I am writing to you.”
en.caption: Many learners say “I write to you to ask about the job.” In Spanish “le escribo para…” uses the simple present, but in an English email we say: “I am writing to you to ask about the job.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
